object_description: three-storey pavilion-like solitaire with cantilevered floor slabs and surrounding arcades
geometry_property: surrounding arcades with external escape stairs
design_condition: the solitaire sits centrally within the perimeter and divides the outdoor space into distinct sub-areas, with a square to the north as a reception area and a partly covered break area to the south merging into the natural landscape

positive: The three-storey, beautifully structured building meets all programme requirements brilliantly in its compactness
The centrally placed solitaire divides the outdoor space into different sub-areas
The surrounding buildings form a square to the north acting as a prelude and reception area
The partly covered break area to the south merges in a staggered manner into the natural outdoor space
The southern outdoor space is understood as a visual reference to the existing school complex
The facility with its natural outdoor space is very well defined and can be experienced
The solitaire has the four separate accesses required in the programme
The clever, pragmatic choice of location for the access road demonstrates the clear architectural approach
The sculptural body with its three cantilevered slabs appears very light, transparent and inviting
The facade is characterised by a layering of three horizontal glass bands and the same three slabs
The surrounding arcades serve as brise-soleil and as escape route
The two external escape staircases remove the need for elaborate internal escape organisation
The four main uses are very clearly separated and easily accessible
The close and transparent connection between school and gymnasium creates a very pleasant feeling of space
The concept of the gymnasium as the core around which the other uses are arranged is very skilfully implemented
The classrooms with group rooms function very well and are lined up in unison on the four facades
The central access on the classroom floor is lit by two atriums
The well-lit learning areas near the atriums have a very high quality of stay
Glass, steel and concrete create a great sense of lightness and a studio-like atmosphere
The structural concept with the school above the hall is an ingenious solution responding precisely to the programme
Wall panels are interrupted where needed by users and structurally possible, an ideal combination of architecture and engineering
The layers of glass bodies and slabs create an outstanding, compact structure reminiscent of a diamond in its clarity
Site planning as well as educational and operational criteria are very well fulfilled
The most impressive entry in terms of architectural quality and suitability for a primary school
negative: Schematic statements on the surroundings convey only an unclear picture of the division of functions and atmospheric quality
The various required building entrances create certain ambiguities regarding orientation on site
The ground floor access from the north via the day structure needs to be reconsidered
Special attention must be paid to airborne noise within the individual uses
